A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAPHIA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDGG and IDGG experiments on three social networks, reward ablations, activity-prediction results, and platform-incentive simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, component and evaluator ablations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces generated behavioral filters with query generation and common-neighbor re-ranking, adds a destination-reward weight, and replaces the category reward's decaying mixture with a fixed GNN term plus an increasing correctness bonus. Appendix C.1 also reports skipping destination-selection SFT, unlike v1, although v2's main text still describes SFT for both agents.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Propagate-En, Weibo Tech, and Weibo Daily under TDGG and IDGG. The same two platform-incentive scenarios remain, moving from Section 4.4 to Appendix D.7. New ablations and timing measurements retain this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated DGGen variants using GraphMixer, DyGFormer, and CAWN, plus a Qwen3-8B version of GAG-General; the original GAG-General matches the retained Llama3-8B version. Its appendix judge comparison adds three DGNN-plus-Qwen3 hybrids and removes Graphia-seq from that particular table, while retaining Graphia-seq elsewhere.

E3.justification: The stated main evaluation judge changes from Qwen3-8B to Qwen2-72B. v2 replaces fixed K1=100 with dataset-specific training candidate counts and replaces epoch schedules with step budgets in Table 5. It also introduces multi-judge, component-control, and timing protocols. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds filtering ablations, four-judge robustness comparisons, an RL-versus-activity-predictor component study, and scalability measurements. It extends the existing Weibo Tech reward ablation to Weibo Daily. The original activity-prediction analysis and platform-incentive case study remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Evaluating multiple judge models in v2 adds robustness evidence rather than statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, ablation, judge, and runtime results. Shared main TDGG values and raw IDGG values remain unchanged, while normalized IDGG scores and rankings change alongside the expanded comparator pool: Graphia's average structure score changes from 0.9574 to 0.9650 and phenomenon score from 0.9141 to 0.9531. These do not establish same-setting performance gains. The displayed v2 phenomenon averages differ by 27.65 percentage points, inconsistent with its reported 28.71% advantage.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a brief complexity argument combining O(N) activity prediction and destination-model training with O(M) edge-model training to claim overall O(M) complexity. No formal proof accompanies it; the original graph formulation and evaluation-score definitions remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central graph-supervised RL framework and micro–macro evaluation contributions remain. Reported headline macro advantages decrease from 41.11% and 32.98% to 35.98% and 28.71%. The abstract drops its counterfactual-simulation claim, although the supporting experiment remains in Appendix D.7.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive interpretations about common-neighbor filtering, activity prediction dominating on larger graphs, and RL contributing more on smaller graphs. It discusses evaluator bias, malformed judge outputs, and computational tradeoffs. The limitations expand causal-policy discussion while removing the explicit qualification that counterfactual tests cover only two one-shot broadcasts.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset-specific RL hyperparameters, difficulty-stratified validation details, hardware and Ray/vLLM information, component timings, and a worked graph-to-prompt example. It additionally states that checkpoints and baseline implementations are available. These disclosures expand reproducibility information, although the previously specified median-distance kernel-bandwidth rule is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting homophily, TGN, CAWN, DyGFormer, and scalability, including EDGE, while removing the Barabasi–Albert reference. It adds positioning against newer temporal-graph methods and an EDGE-inspired complexity discussion. The central related-work argument remains largely unchanged; many other reference edits concern formatting.

P1.justification: The introduction and limitations are revised, method explanations receive localized edits, and acknowledgments are added. Appendix D is reorganized, including moving platform incentives from Section 4.4 to D.7. The main section sequence and much existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1's destination-selection panel and reward displays, expands the main IDGG and appendix judge tables, and adds six tables covering hyperparameters and supplementary experiments. Dataset blocks are reordered, aggregate plots updated, and the incentive figure relocated to the appendix. These extend beyond numerical substitutions or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added DGNN/hybrid comparisons, alternative judges, and filtering/RL/activity-predictor controls address important gaps in v1's evidence and make the paper easier to assess. Expanded implementation details also help. The net gain is limited by inconsistent SFT/filter descriptions, conflicting echo-chamber results in Tables 3 and 14, and claimed runtime advantages without displayed GAG-General timings in Table 15.
